narrative:
Based on the information you provided, our model estimates there is a 59% chance that you would be a bad credit risk. That means the risk of you failing to repay the loan is higher than the bank’s acceptable threshold, so your application was denied.

The three most important reasons for this decision, in order of influence, were the length of the loan, the status of your checking account, and the loan amount itself.

Your requested loan duration of 48 months was the strongest factor pushing the decision toward denial. Approved applicants typically request loans for around 19 months on average, so your request is roughly two and a half times longer. Longer repayment periods create more uncertainty about your future ability to pay.

Your checking account status also worked against you. Your account was overdrawn (below zero DM) at the time of the application. Among approved applicants, only about 13% had a negative balance, so this is a clear sign of current financial strain.

Interestingly, the loan amount actually had a counterbalancing effect, nudging the prediction slightly toward “good credit.” While you requested 4,308 DM, which is above the average of about 3,020 DM among approved applicants, the model did not treat the amount itself as the problem. It was the combination of the long term and existing account stress that drove the denial.

To improve your chances in the future, consider asking for a shorter loan period and working to bring your checking account balance into positive territory. Demonstrating steady repayment over time will also help you build a stronger credit profile.
